entries.title: Variance fluctuation exponent in a fixed direction
entries.statement: For a sequence of real random variables T_n with 0<Var(T_n)<infinity, its variance fluctuation exponent is chi_var=lim_{n->infinity} log Var(T_n)/(2 log n), if this limit exists. This definition concerns variance only; it does not assert a weak limiting law or equivalence to a typical-fluctuation or transversal exponent.
assumptions: The limit is asserted only when it exists

entries.title: DRAFT conditional weak-scaling to variance bridge
entries.statement: DRAFT concept; independent mathematical KEEP by w371; integration pending. Let X_n be real with 0<sigma_n^2=Var(X_n)<infinity and E|X_n-EX_n|^4<=K sigma_n^4 for one finite K and every n. For positive a_n and deterministic m_n, if (X_n-m_n)/a_n converges weakly to a nondegenerate real Z, then Z has finite positive variance and Var(X_n)/a_n^2 converges to Var(Z). No independence across n is required. The proof is recorded in the campaign audit; neither this moment condition nor n^(1/3) nondegenerate weak scaling has been established here for iid planar lattice FPP.
assumptions: One uniform standardized fourth-moment constant K
Nondegenerate weak limit at the asserted scale

entries.title: Refuted candidate replacement of moment control by larger-scale concentration
entries.statement: DRAFT refuted route. The candidate inference says that nondegenerate n^(1/3) weak scaling, a uniform exponential tail bound for centered fluctuations at sqrt(n/log n), and a variance upper bound C n/log n force variance exponent 1/3. This inference is false for arbitrary random-variable sequences; the rare-event countermodel in this bundle satisfies those premises and has variance exponent 3/8. No claim of an iid lattice FPP counterexample is made.
assumptions: Abstract random-variable sequences, not a lattice model

entries.title: DRAFT rare-event obstruction retaining subdiffusive-scale tails
entries.statement: DRAFT concept; independent mathematical KEEP by w371; integration pending. For n>=4, put a_n=n^(1/3), s_n=sqrt(n/log n), and p_n=n^(-1/4). Let Z,S be independent symmetric signs and B_n an independent Bernoulli(p_n). Set Q_n=n+a_n Z+s_n B_n S. Then (Q_n-n)/a_n converges weakly to a symmetric sign, Var(Q_n)=n^(2/3)+n^(3/4)/log n, and chi_var=3/8. Moreover P(|Q_n-EQ_n|>=t s_n)<=exp(2.1-t) for every t>=0, Var(Q_n)<=(3/e+1)n/log n, and the standardized fourth moment is asymptotic to n^(1/4). These are abstract sequence statements and do not establish or refute lattice KPZ.
assumptions: Independence of the signs and Bernoulli variable for each n

entries.title: DRAFT quantified anti-concentration implies a variance lower bound
entries.statement: DRAFT concept; w369 proof audited by w370, referee w371 pending. If a real square-integrable X satisfies P(X in I)<=1-epsilon for every closed interval I of one fixed length L>0, with epsilon in (0,1], then Var(X)>=epsilon L^2/4. Apply the assumption to the interval centered at EX and integrate squared deviations outside it. A variance lower bound alone does not imply such uniform anti-concentration. This corrects the categorical logical explanation on recalled card claim_3ccc6fc493b4e17b5c29966949004f575c51205c8a4f0ba3bc516d0b752ebea4, without restating the cited paper theorem.
assumptions: The bound holds for every interval of the same positive length
